title: South Korea hopes for talks between US and North Korea after Trump downsizes military drills
gist: AP reports that after Trump ordered a cutback of the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea, citing his rapport with Kim Jong Un and Seoul's refusal to back the Iran war, South Korea says it hopes the move spurs US-North Korea diplomacy, though experts including CNAS's Duyeon Kim warn the drawdown weakens alliance readiness while Kim is unlikely to return to talks without major concessions.

insights.claim: Trump ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to 'substantially reduce' the annual U.S.-South Korea military exercises, saying in a social media post that the drills are costly and 'send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile' toward North Korea, which he said 'has been unthreatening and respectful' during his time in office.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.quote: send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile
insights.locator: Trump orders military to 'substantially reduce' drills

insights.claim: Trump said he asked South Korean President Lee Jae Myung whether Seoul would join the U.S. in the 'denuclearization' of Iran, and that Lee responded 'No thanks!', explicitly linking the drill cutback to South Korea's refusal to support the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Directly ties a major Indo-Pacific alliance decision to an unrelated Middle East conflict, illustrating how Trump links regional commitments together as leverage.
insights.locator: He added that he recently asked President Lee Jae Myung

insights.claim: Trump said Kim Jong Un treats him with 'great respect,' signaling a likely bid to re-engage North Korea diplomatically via the goodwill gesture of reduced drills.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.locator: President Donald Trump said Monday that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un treats him

insights.claim: This is not the first time Trump has moved to suspend the drills: after his first 2018 summit with Kim, he unilaterally suspended the summertime exercises, calling them 'very provocative' and 'tremendously expensive,' the same rationale he is using now.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Establishes a repeatable pattern in Trump's North Korea policy playbook, useful for forecasting future drill or exercise decisions under his administration.

insights.claim: Duyeon Kim, a senior analyst at CNAS, said 'reducing joint drills weakens military readiness over time against another potential North Korean attack.'
insights.speaker: Duyeon Kim (CNAS), via Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.quote: reducing joint drills weakens military readiness over time against another potential North Korean attack.

insights.claim: Duyeon Kim also said North Korea uses the U.S.-South Korea drills 'for domestic propaganda purposes to create a false narrative of a hostile America and justify its nuclear weapons program,' implying the drills' deterrent value must be weighed against their propaganda utility to Pyongyang.

insights.claim: Leif-Eric Easley of Ewha University argues North Korea 'is busy profiting from Russia's war against Ukraine while modernizing its own military,' and that downsizing the drills 'can damage alliance coordination, slow the process of South Korea taking on greater responsibility for its own defense, and weaken deterrence against possible conflicts in Asia.'
insights.speaker: Leif-Eric Easley, via Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Frames drill downsizing as having compounding negative effects on alliance burden-sharing progress, not just immediate deterrence.
insights.quote: can damage alliance coordination, slow the process of South Korea taking on greater responsibility for its own defense, and weaken deterrence against possible conflicts in Asia.

insights.claim: Experts say Kim Jong Un, emboldened by his advancing nuclear arsenal and expanding military cooperation with Russia, is unlikely to return to talks unless assured of serious U.S. concessions.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Sets a high bar for any near-term US-North Korea diplomatic breakthrough despite Trump's overture, tempering expectations of a quick deal.
insights.locator: experts say the North Korean leader, now emboldened by his advancing nuclear arsenal

insights.claim: In September 2025, Kim suggested he could resume talks with Trump if the U.S. drops 'its delusional obsession with denuclearization' of North Korea; experts believe Kim aims to leverage his enlarged nuclear arsenal for major concessions such as extensive sanctions relief.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Clarifies North Korea's actual negotiating precondition and end goal, useful for assessing the odds and likely shape of any future US-NK deal.
insights.locator: In September 2025, Kim suggested he could resume talks

insights.claim: Kim Dong-yub of the University of North Korean Studies said North Korea feels less urgency to return to talks now than in 2018, but is unlikely to completely ignore Trump's overture, predicting Pyongyang will acknowledge Trump's post while waiting for further concrete action before engaging.
insights.speaker: Kim Dong-yub, via Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Frames the most likely near-term outcome as a wait-and-see stance from Pyongyang rather than immediate re-engagement or outright rejection.

insights.claim: South Korea and the U.S. are closely discussing practical and military contributions Seoul could make to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, indicating Seoul may offer support elsewhere even as it declines direct involvement in the Iran war.

insights.so_what: A concrete potential South Korean military or logistics commitment to watch, which could partly offset friction from Seoul's refusal to join the Iran 'denuclearization' push.

insights.claim: President Lee Jae Myung, a liberal favoring improved inter-Korean ties, has taken steps like turning off frontline loudspeakers broadcasting K-pop and news into North Korea and offered talks to formally end the 1950-53 Korean War (still only under armistice), drawing criticism from the conservative opposition People Power Party for allegedly ignoring public security concerns.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Shows a growing domestic South Korean political divide over inter-Korean engagement policy that could shape future alliance-cooperation levels regardless of Trump's decisions.
insights.locator: Lee is a liberal who espouses improved ties with North Korea

insights.claim: The 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises began as scheduled, involving about 18,000 South Korean soldiers and incorporating lessons from North Korea's battlefield experience on the Russia-Ukraine front, including live-fire, wet-gap-crossing, and prepositioned-equipment-distribution drills; it was not yet known which parts would be downsized.
insights.speaker: Hyung-Jin Kim
insights.so_what: Establishes the concrete scale and scope of the exercise being cut, providing a baseline against which to measure the eventual downsizing.
